summary.text: The received graph is analyzed as 土 contributing meaning and 才 supplying sound. Its early construction is disputed: accounts differ over whether it included 士 and how that element relates to 土.

formation.text: The Han dictionary parses the received form as 土 plus phonetic 才, a phonosemantic analysis. Early forms have competing explanations: one account treats 才 and 士 as sound elements; other accounts describe 才 as a sign reused to write 在, with 土 or 士 added later. The evidence does not establish a complete graphic sequence.

components.text: The Han dictionary parses the received graph with 土 as its meaning element. Accounts differ over whether early forms already contained 土 or instead contained 士.

In the received-form analysis, 才 supplies the sound. Accounts differ on whether it occurred alongside 士 or was first used to write 在 as a whole. 才’s own ancient referent is disputed between sprout and stake-or-pile interpretations.

sound.text: The Baxter–Sagart Middle Chinese forms are similar, though their ending notation differs; this supports the proposed sound role.
The Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms share similar initial and rime material, though their ending notation differs; this fits but does not prove the proposed sound role.
Mandarin 才 and 在 have similar finals but different initials and tones; this present-day comparison does not establish their ancient sound relation.

components.text: One account analyzes early forms as containing 士, a proposed second sound element, later confused with 土. This role is disputed; the cited Baxter–Sagart comparison does not independently support it.

sound_limitation.text: The reported Baxter–Sagart forms for 士 and 在 differ substantially, so they do not independently establish the proposed sound role.

sound.text: The reported forms differ substantially in this system; this comparison does not independently support the proposed role.
The reported Old Chinese forms differ substantially in this system; this comparison does not independently support the proposed role.
Mandarin 士 and 在 are shì and zài; this current-reading comparison does not establish an ancient sound relation.

history.text: The Han dictionary parses the received graph as 土 plus phonetic 才. This is a historical dictionary analysis, not proof of the earliest construction.

Accounts of early forms conflict. One analyzes them as 才 plus 士 and says 士 and 土 became confused after the Spring and Autumn/Warring States period. Other accounts describe 才 reused to write 在, followed by a later addition of 土 or 士; they do not establish a complete, dated sequence.
A reported bronze inscription uses 在 for the separate word 士. The supplied evidence does not establish whether this reuse was based on similar pronunciation.

uncertainties.text: The earliest graphic construction is disputed: accounts differ over whether early forms included 士 or 才 was first used alone before another element was added.
One account proposes 士 as a second sound element, but the cited Baxter–Sagart comparison does not independently support this role.
才’s ancient referent and the name or pronunciation of that object remain unsettled; no borrowing based on the object’s name is established.
Reported inscription readings support early uses, but the examples do not establish a complete chronology among location, existence, and “formerly.”
A proposed relation between 在 and 栽 is described as probable, but the other supplied evidence does not substantiate it.

senses.gloss: be at; be in; be located
senses.period: Shang oracle-bone and bronze usage reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: A reported oracle-bone date phrase uses 才, read as 在, in the sense “in”; reported bronze examples also show a locative use. The evidence supports an early locative or temporal use, though the phrase’s exact date and reading remain unresolved.

senses.period: Early bronze usage reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Reported bronze uses include existence and location; the Han dictionary glosses 在 as 存, “exist” or “be present.” The evidence does not establish when this sense arose relative to locative use.

senses.period: Bronze usage reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: A reported bronze example uses 才 read as 在 in a past-time expression. The evidence does not establish a semantic path from the locative or existence uses to this use.

senses.gloss: be at, in, or on; consist in; rest
senses.text: Current definitions include being at, in, or on a place, as well as consist in and rest. These glosses do not establish the chronology or derivation of historical senses.

limitations.text: The reported early examples do not establish exact dates, priority among senses, or transitions between location, existence, and “formerly”; no semantic chain is inferred from dictionary gloss order.
A separate bronze inscription records 在 used for 士. The supplied evidence does not determine the mechanism behind this use or provide a sound comparison for the two words.

overview.text: 在 commonly means being present or located somewhere, including “be at” or “be in.” One account proposes that 才 was reused to write 在 because the words sounded alike; this proposed sound match remains unestablished, and 才’s old object-name is unknown.

components.text: In the received-form analysis, 土 contributes meaning; accounts differ about its relation to 士 in early forms.
才 supplies the sound in the received-form analysis. Baxter–Sagart forms share similar initial and rime material, though their ending notation differs.
One disputed account places 士 in the early graph as a proposed second sound element.

relationships.text: The historical dictionary analyzes the received graph as 土 plus 才, with 土 as the meaning element. This does not establish 土’s role in the earliest form.
The received-form analysis assigns 才 the sound role, and Baxter–Sagart’s comparisons are compatible with it. Early graphic accounts differ over 才’s placement and history.
One account proposes 士 as a second sound element in early forms. Its reported Baxter–Sagart readings differ substantially from 在 and do not independently support that role.

A reported oracle-bone date phrase uses 才, read as 在, in the sense “in”; reported bronze examples also show a locative use. The evidence supports an early locative or temporal use, though the phrase’s exact date and reading remain unresolved.
Reported bronze uses include existence and location; the Han dictionary glosses 在 as 存, “exist” or “be present.” The evidence does not establish when this sense arose relative to locative use.
A reported bronze example uses 才 read as 在 in a past-time expression. The evidence does not establish a semantic path from the locative or existence uses to this use.
Current definitions include being at, in, or on a place, as well as consist in and rest. These glosses do not establish the chronology or derivation of historical senses.

limitations.text: No verifiable glyph image is available to illustrate 在’s debated early forms: the identified oracle-script and seal-script images could not be retrieved, and no alternative exact image with verified reuse terms was established. The written accounts also disagree about whether early forms used 才 alone or 才 with 士, so the graphic sequence remains uncertain.
